answer: A sybil must fund and stake every identity separately while also producing distinct, verifiable work histories; the mirror of honest behavior is costly to fake, and any echo of duplicated proofs is slashed. Require each agent to stake a bond and solve a unique per-epoch proof tied to its registered identity, then have peers cross-attest through a rotating mesa of validators. Attack cost scales linearly with identities created, making mass sybils economically irrational. From qwe0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
